biography.plain_text: Jerry Seinfeld is an American comedian and actor who co-created Seinfeld with Larry David. Raised on Long Island, he developed his stand-up act in New York clubs before reaching a national audience on The Tonight Show. His share of the sitcom's licensing income underpins a fortune built through writing, performing and producing.

long_biography.plain_text:
American comedian Jerry Seinfeld develops new material on yellow legal pads, working from notebooks of observations about ordinary behaviour. He separates invention from revision, adjusting individual words until a passage sounds right to him. Performing it supplies another test: audience reactions determine what he rewrites, keeps or discards.

His fascination with Pop-Tarts eventually became Unfrosted, which he co-wrote, directed and starred in. He and Spike Feresten had joked about making a film on the subject before beginning the screenplay during the pandemic. They borrowed the competitive structure of The Right Stuff for a comedy about rival cereal companies racing to invent a breakfast pastry.
